questions.question: What does the presence of parallel straight magnetic field lines inside a solenoid indicate?

options.text: The magnetic field is non-uniform and changes at different points
The magnetic field is zero inside the solenoid
The magnetic field is infinite inside the solenoid
The magnetic field is uniform inside the solenoid

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The magnetic field is uniform inside the solenoid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **solenoid** is defined as a coil consisting of **many circular turns** of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder.
 
• When an electric **current** flows through a solenoid, it produces a magnetic field around and inside it. The magnetic field lines inside the solenoid are in the form of **parallel straight lines**.
 
• The presence of these **parallel straight lines** indicates that the **magnetic field is uniform** inside the solenoid. This means the **magnitude and direction** of the magnetic field are the **same** at all points within the interior of the solenoid. ***Hence, the correct option is the magnetic field is uniform inside the solenoid.***
 
• The magnetic field lines of a **current-carrying solenoid** resemble the pattern of magnetic field lines produced by a **bar magnet**, where one end acts as a **North pole** and the other as a **South pole**.
 
• The **uniformity** of the field is a characteristic of an **ideal** or long solenoid, where the length is much greater than the diameter, ensuring the field lines remain **equidistant and parallel**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors Affecting Magnetic Field Strength**: The strength of the **magnetic field (B)** inside a solenoid depends on several factors, including the **number of turns per unit length (n)** and the **magnitude of the current (I)** passing through the wire. Increasing either of these will increase the **magnetic field intensity**.
 
• **Electromagnets**: A strong, uniform magnetic field inside a solenoid can be utilized to magnetize **ferromagnetic materials**, such as a **soft iron core**. When a soft iron rod is placed inside the solenoid, it becomes an **electromagnet**, which retains its magnetism only as long as the **current** flows.
 
• **Polarity and Direction**: The direction of the magnetic field lines **outside** the solenoid is from the **North pole to the South pole**, whereas **inside** the solenoid, the direction is from the **South pole to the North pole**, forming continuous **closed loops**.
 
• **Zero Field Outside**: In the case of an **ideal solenoid** that is infinitely long, the magnetic field **outside** the coil is considered to be **zero** because the field lines cancel each other out or spread to infinity.
 
• **Right-Hand Thumb Rule**: This rule can be used to determine the direction of the magnetic field. If the fingers of the **right hand** are curled in the direction of the **current** in the turns, the **thumb** points toward the **North pole** of the solenoid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Applications**: Solenoids are widely used in **engineering** and **physics** as **actuators**, **valves**, and **switches**. They are fundamental components in **car starters**, **doorbell mechanisms**, and **industrial controls**.
 
• **Material Core**: The use of a **soft iron core** significantly enhances the magnetic flux compared to an **air-core solenoid**, making the device much more powerful for **lifting heavy loads** or **relay operations**.
 
• **Discovery**: The term "solenoid" was coined by the **French physicist André-Marie Ampère** in the year **1823** to describe a helical coil.

questions.question: In uniform circular motion, the direction of velocity of an object is:

options.text: Along the radius, toward the center
Perpendicular to the axis of rotation
Along the radius, away from the center

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tangential to the circular path**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Uniform Circular Motion (UCM)**, an object travels along a circular path at a **constant speed**. However, since velocity is a **vector quantity**, it involves both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
• The **direction of velocity** at any point in the circular path is always **tangential** to the circle at that specific point. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The velocity vector is always **perpendicular (at a 90-degree angle)** to the **radius** of the circular path. This ensures that the motion is always directed along the curve.
 
• Even though the **speed** remains constant in **UCM**, the continuous change in the **direction of velocity** means the object is constantly **accelerating**.
 
• A practical example is a stone tied to a string and whirled in a circle; if the string breaks, the stone will fly off in a **straight line** along the **tangent** to the circle at the point where it was released.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Centripetal Acceleration:**

 
 
• While velocity is tangential, the **acceleration** in uniform circular motion is directed **radially inward**, toward the **center** of the circle.
 
• This is known as **centripetal acceleration**, and its magnitude is given by the formula **a = v²/r**, where **v** is linear velocity and **r** is the radius. ***Hence, statement 1 describes acceleration, not velocity.***
 
 
 
• **Centripetal Force:**
 
 
• According to **Newton's Second Law**, an inward acceleration requires an inward force. This force is called **centripetal force** (**F = mv²/r**).
 
• In the case of a planet orbiting a star, the **gravitational force** provides the necessary centripetal force to maintain circular motion.
 
 
 
• **Angular Velocity (ω):**
 
 
• The rate at which the object rotates around the center is called **angular velocity**.
 
• The relationship between **linear velocity (v)** and **angular velocity (ω)** is defined by the equation **v = rω**.
 
 
 
• **Displacement and Distance:**
 
 
• In one complete revolution, the **distance** covered by the object is equal to the **circumference** of the circle (**2πr**).
 
• However, the **net displacement** of the object after one full **360-degree** rotation is **zero**, as the object returns to its original starting position.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Direction of Motion:** In circular motion, the **direction of motion** is the same as the **direction of velocity**.
 
• **Axis of Rotation:** The **axis of rotation** is an imaginary line around which the object rotates. In two-dimensional circular motion, the velocity is **perpendicular** to the **radius** but stays within the **plane of rotation**. ***Hence, statement 2 is partially descriptive of the plane but does not define the specific direction of velocity.***
 
• **Centrifugal "Force":** From the frame of reference of the rotating object, an outward "force" called **centrifugal force** is often felt, but in an **inertial frame**, only the **inward centripetal force** exists. ***Hence, statement 3 (away from center) describes the fictitious centrifugal effect, not the velocity.***

questions.question: What is the best way to manage non-biodegradable waste such as plastic?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Recycle and reuse it**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-biodegradable waste** refers to materials that cannot be broken down or decomposed by **natural agents** such as **bacteria**, **fungi**, or **biological processes** over time. **Plastic**, **glass**, and **metal scraps** are prominent examples.
 
• **Recycle and reuse it** is the most sustainable and effective method for managing **plastic waste**. **Recycling** involves processing used materials into new products to prevent the waste of potentially useful materials, while **reusing** involves using an item multiple times for the same or a different purpose. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 4.***
 
• **Burying plastic in soil** (landfilling) is highly detrimental as it leads to **soil pollution**. Since plastic does not decompose for **hundreds of years**, it creates a barrier in the soil that prevents the **seepage of rainwater** into the ground, affecting **groundwater recharge**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Burning plastic in open air** (incineration without controls) releases extremely toxic chemicals like **dioxins**, **furans**, **mercury**, and **polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs)** into the **atmosphere**. These pollutants are hazardous to **human health** and contribute significantly to **air pollution** and the **greenhouse effect**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Mixing plastic with compost** is not a viable solution because **composting** is a biological process meant only for **organic/biodegradable waste**. Plastic does not turn into **humus**; instead, it contaminates the **compost** with **microplastics** and **chemical additives**, making it unfit for **agricultural use**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The 3 R's Hierarchy**: The waste management hierarchy follows the order of **Reduce**, **Reuse**, and **Recycle**. **Reducing** consumption is the most effective, followed by **reusing** items to extend their **life cycle**, and finally **recycling** to recover **raw materials**.
 
• **Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016 (India)**: These rules were notified by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** to mandate **waste segregation** at the source and promote the use of **plastic waste** in **road construction** or **energy recovery**.
 
• **Single-Use Plastic Ban**: In **India**, a ban on identified **single-use plastic** items, which have low utility and high littering potential, came into effect on **July 1, 2022**. This includes items like **plastic sticks for balloons**, **plastic flags**, and **thermocol**.
 
• **Microplastics**: These are plastic particles smaller than **5 millimeters**. They result from the **fragmentation** of larger plastic waste and pose a severe threat to **marine ecosystems** and the **human food chain**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR)**: This is a policy approach under which **producers** are given a significant responsibility—financial and/or physical—for the **treatment or disposal** of post-consumer products.
 
• **Circular Economy**: This concept aims to redefine growth, focusing on positive society-wide benefits. It entails **decoupling economic activity** from the consumption of finite resources and **designing waste out** of the system through **recycling**.
 
• **Waste Segregation**: Effective recycling is only possible through **source segregation** where **dry waste** (plastic, paper, metal) is kept separate from **wet waste** (kitchen waste) and **domestic hazardous waste**.
 
• **Biodegradable Plastics**: Scientists are developing **bioplastics** derived from renewable biomass sources, like **vegetable fats and oils** or **corn starch**, which can decompose much faster than conventional **petroleum-based plastics**.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red blood cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **tissue** is a group of **similar cells** that work together to perform a specific function. The study of tissues is known as **Histology**.
 
• **Nerves** are primarily composed of **nervous tissue**, which consists of **neurons** (nerve cells) and **neuroglia**. They are responsible for transmitting **electrical impulses** throughout the body. ***Hence, statement 1 is a tissue.***
 
• **Red blood cells (Erythrocytes)** are individual **cells** produced in the **bone marrow**. While they are a major component of blood, they are considered **single cells** rather than a tissue on their own. ***Hence, statement 2 is NOT a tissue.***
 
• **Muscles** consist of **muscular tissue**, which is characterized by the ability to **contract** and **relax**, enabling movement. It is one of the four primary tissue types in animals. ***Hence, statement 3 is a tissue.***
 
• **Blood** is uniquely classified as a **fluid connective tissue**. It is considered a tissue because it consists of a group of specialized cells (RBCs, WBCs, and platelets) that originate from a common source and function together within the **plasma**. ***Hence, statement 4 is a tissue.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Animal Tissues:**

 
 
• **Epithelial Tissue:** Acts as a **protective layer** covering the body surface and lining internal organs (e.g., **skin**, **inner lining of the mouth**).
 
• **Connective Tissue:** Supports, binds, and protects other tissues and organs. Examples include **bone**, **cartilage**, **tendons**, and **blood**.
 
• **Muscular Tissue:** Responsible for **locomotion** and movement. It is divided into **skeletal**, **smooth**, and **cardiac** muscles.
 
• **Nervous Tissue:** Forms the **brain**, **spinal cord**, and **nerves**. It specialized in communication using **electrochemical signals**.
 
 
 
• **Red Blood Cells (RBCs):**
 
 
• They are **biconcave** in shape and lack a **nucleus** at maturity in humans to provide more space for **hemoglobin**.
 
• Their primary function is the transport of **oxygen** from the lungs to the tissues and **carbon dioxide** back to the lungs.
 
• The average lifespan of a human RBC is approximately **120 days**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Levels of Organization:** In biological systems, the hierarchy of complexity begins with the **cell** (the basic unit of life). A group of cells forms a **tissue**, multiple tissues form an **organ** (like the heart or lungs), and organs work together in an **organ system** (like the circulatory system).
 
• **Why Blood is a Tissue:** Although liquid, blood meets the criteria for a tissue because it has a **matrix** (plasma) and specific **cellular components** (erythrocytes, leukocytes, and thrombocytes) that work collectively for **transportation**, **protection**, and **regulation**.
 
• **Histology Origins:** The term "tissue" was introduced by **Marie François Xavier Bichat** in the late **18th century**, who is often regarded as the **Father of Histology**.

questions.question: In the reaction {CuO} + {H}₂ rightarrow {Cu} + {H}₂{O} , which substance is oxidised?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given chemical equation **CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O** represents a classic **redox (reduction-oxidation)** reaction where both oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously.
 
• **Oxidation** is defined as the chemical process where a substance **gains oxygen** or **loses hydrogen**. In this reaction, the **Hydrogen (H2)** molecule reacts with **Copper oxide (CuO)** and gains an oxygen atom to form **Water (H2O)**.
 
• Because **Hydrogen** is the species that acquires oxygen during the chemical change, it is the substance that is **oxidised**.
 
• **Reduction**, conversely, is the process where a substance **loses oxygen** or **gains hydrogen**. Here, **Copper oxide (CuO)** loses its oxygen atom to be converted into **metallic Copper (Cu)**.
 
• Since **Copper oxide** undergoes the loss of oxygen, it is identified as the substance being **reduced** in this chemical interaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Oxidizing and Reducing Agents**:

 
 
• An **oxidizing agent** is a substance that facilitates oxidation by providing oxygen or accepting electrons. In this reaction, **Copper oxide (CuO)** is the **oxidizing agent** because it provides the oxygen required for the oxidation of hydrogen.
 
• A **reducing agent** is a substance that facilitates reduction by removing oxygen or donating electrons. **Hydrogen (H2)** acts as the **reducing agent** here because it removes the oxygen from the copper oxide.
 
 
 
• **Electronic Concept of Redox**:
 
 
• In modern chemistry, oxidation is also defined as the **loss of electrons** (increase in oxidation state), while reduction is the **gain of electrons** (decrease in oxidation state).
 
• In the reaction **CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O**, the **Copper** ion in **CuO** has an oxidation state of **+2** and is reduced to **0** in metallic **Cu**. The **Hydrogen** atom has an oxidation state of **0** in **H2** and is oxidised to **+1** in **H2O**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Redox Reactions**:
 
 
• These reactions are fundamental to **metallurgical processes**, such as the **extraction of metals** from their ores (e.g., using carbon or hydrogen to reduce metal oxides).
 
• They are also essential in **biological systems** for energy production (cellular respiration) and in everyday phenomena like **combustion**, **rusting of iron**, and the functioning of **batteries**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nature of the Reactants**: **Copper oxide (CuO)** is typically a **black solid**, while **metallic Copper (Cu)** formed after reduction appears as a **reddish-brown** substance. This visible change in color is a key indicator that a chemical reaction has taken place.
 
• **Role of Heat**: This specific reaction generally requires **heating** the copper oxide in a stream of hydrogen gas to proceed at a measurable rate, making it an **endothermic** process in terms of activation energy.
 
• **Water Formation**: The **Water (H2O)** produced in this reaction is often released in the form of **steam** or water vapor due to the heat applied during the process.
 
• **Hydrogen as a Reducer**: Hydrogen is a powerful **reducing agent** capable of reducing the oxides of many metals that are less reactive than hydrogen in the **reactivity series**, such as lead, silver, and copper.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the absolute refractive index?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is always greater than 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **absolute refractive index** of a medium is defined as the ratio of the **speed of light in a vacuum** to the **speed of light in that specific medium**.
 
• It is mathematically expressed by the formula **n = c / v**, where **n** is the absolute refractive index, **c** is the speed of light in a vacuum (approximately **3 x 10⁸ meters per second**), and **v** is the speed of light in the medium.
 
• According to the laws of physics, **light travels at its maximum speed in a vacuum**. In any other material medium (like water, glass, or oil), light interacts with atoms and slows down, meaning the value of **v** is always less than **c**.
 
• Because the numerator (**c**) is always larger than the denominator (**v**), the ratio will always result in a value **greater than 1** for all physical media. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The refractive index of a **vacuum** is exactly **1**. For all other substances, it is higher. For example, the refractive index of **air** is about **1.0003**, which is extremely close to 1 but still greater. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The refractive index represents a ratio of two speeds, which means the units cancel out, making it a **dimensionless** and **unitless** quantity. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• In natural materials, the refractive index is always **positive**. While scientists have engineered "metamaterials" that can have a **negative refractive index** under specific lab conditions, in the context of standard optics, it is not negative. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Optical Density:** A medium with a **higher refractive index** is referred to as **optically denser**, whereas a medium with a **lower refractive index** is **optically rarer**. When light enters a denser medium, its speed decreases and it bends toward the **normal**.
 
• **Common Refractive Indices:**
 
 
• **Water:** Approximately **1.33**.
 
• **Crown Glass:** Approximately **1.52**.
 
• **Diamond:** Approximately **2.42**, which is one of the highest among natural substances, contributing to its extreme sparkling and total internal reflection.
 
 
 
• **Snell's Law:** The refractive index is used in **Snell's Law of Refraction**, which states that **n1 sin(i) = n2 sin(r)**, where **i** is the angle of incidence and **r** is the angle of refraction.
 
• **Relative Refractive Index:** This refers to the ratio of the speed of light in **medium 1** to the speed of light in **medium 2**. Unlike the absolute refractive index, a **relative refractive index** can be less than 1 if light moves from a denser medium to a rarer one.
 
• **Factors of Influence:** The refractive index of a material depends on the **temperature**, the **nature of the material**, and the **wavelength of light** (a phenomenon known as **dispersion**, which causes rainbows).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Speed of Light:** In a vacuum, light travels at **299,792,458 meters per second**. For general calculations, this is rounded to **3 x 10⁸ m/s**.
 
• **Relationship with Wavelength:** Since the frequency of light remains **constant** when changing media, a change in speed results in a change in **wavelength**. The refractive index is also the ratio of the wavelength in a vacuum to the wavelength in the medium (**n = λ_vacuum / λ_medium**).
 
• **Significance:** The concept of refractive index is vital in designing **lenses**, **microscopes**, **telescopes**, and **fiber optic cables** used in modern high-speed internet.

questions.question: From a distance–time graph, an object moves from point A to point B, covering a distance (s₂ - s₁) in time (t₂ - t₁) . Which of the following correctly represents the speed (v) of the object?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**v = (s2 - s1)/(t2 - t1)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **speed** of an object is defined as the **rate of change of distance** with respect to **time**. Mathematically, it is expressed as **v = Distance / Time**.
 
• On a **distance-time graph**, the **distance (s)** is typically represented on the **vertical axis (y-axis)**, and the **time (t)** is represented on the **horizontal axis (x-axis)**.
 
• When an object moves from **point A** to **point B**, the change in distance is given by **(s2 - s1)**, which represents the **total path length** covered between those two points.
 
• The duration or **time interval** taken to cover this distance is calculated as **(t2 - t1)**.
 
• The **slope** of the line joining points A and B on a **distance-time graph** represents the **speed (v)** of the object. Therefore, the formula is **v = (s2 - s1) / (t2 - t1)**. ***Hence, the statement represented by option 1 is correct.***
 
• The unit of speed in the **International System of Units (SI)** is **meters per second (m/s)**, although it is often expressed in **km/h** for vehicles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uniform and Non-Uniform Motion:**

 
 
• In **uniform motion**, an object covers **equal distances** in **equal intervals of time**, resulting in a **straight line** on a distance-time graph.
 
• In **non-uniform motion**, the distance-time graph is a **curve**, indicating that the **speed** is changing at different points in time.
 
 
 
• **Speed vs. Velocity:**
 
 
• While **speed** is a **scalar quantity** (only magnitude), **velocity** is a **vector quantity** that includes both **magnitude and direction**.
 
• The **slope** of a **displacement-time graph** gives the **velocity**, whereas the slope of a **distance-time graph** gives the **speed**.
 
 
 
• **Instantaneous Speed:**
 
 
• The speed of an object at any **particular instant of time** is called **instantaneous speed**. In a graph, this is found by calculating the **slope of the tangent** at that specific point.
 
 
 
• **Average Speed:**
 
 
• **Average speed** is the **total distance** traveled divided by the **total time taken**. The formula **v = (s2 - s1) / (t2 - t1)** effectively calculates the average speed between two specific time coordinates.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Graph Interpretation:**

 
 
• If the **distance-time graph** is a **horizontal line** (parallel to the time axis), the speed is **zero**, meaning the object is at **rest**.
 
• A **steeper slope** on the graph indicates a **higher speed**, as more distance is being covered in less time.
 
• A **distance-time graph** can never have a **negative slope** because **distance** is a cumulative quantity that never decreases with time, unlike **displacement**.
 
 
 
• **Mathematical Relations:**
 
 
• The expression **(s2 - s1)** is often denoted as **delta s (Δs)** and **(t2 - t1)** as **delta t (Δt)**. Thus, **v = Δs / Δt**.
 
• This relationship is fundamental in **kinematics** and is used to derive further equations of motion under **constant acceleration**.

questions.question: Which feature is common to all solids?

options.text: Easily compressible structure when pressure applied
Definite volume and shape under normal conditions
Ability to flow like liquids in open containers
Infinite expansion capability with added energy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Definite volume and shape under normal conditions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Solids** are defined by their **structural rigidity** and resistance to changes in shape or volume. Unlike liquids or gases, the constituent particles (atoms, molecules, or ions) in a solid are **closely packed** together.
 
• One of the most fundamental **features** of all solids is that they possess a **definite shape and a definite volume**. This is due to the **strong intermolecular forces** of attraction that hold the particles in **fixed positions**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Solids are generally **incompressible**. Because the particles are already so close to each other, applying **pressure** does not significantly reduce the volume. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Solids do not have the **ability to flow**. Fluidity is a characteristic of **liquids and gases**, where particles can slide past one another. In solids, particles only **vibrate** around their **mean positions**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• While solids can expand when heated (**thermal expansion**), they do not have **infinite expansion capability**. This property is characteristic of **gases**, which expand to fill the entire volume of any container they occupy. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Solids:**

 
 
• **Crystalline Solids:** These have a **regular, repeating three-dimensional pattern** of particles. Examples include **diamond**, **quartz**, and **sodium chloride (salt)**. They typically have **sharp melting points**.
 
• **Amorphous Solids:** These lack a long-range ordered structure. Examples include **glass**, **rubber**, and many **plastics**. They soften over a **range of temperatures** rather than melting at a specific **numerical value**.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Molecular Theory:**
 
 
• In the **solid state**, the **kinetic energy** of the particles is at its **lowest** compared to the liquid or gaseous states.
 
• The particles are held together by various types of bonds, such as **ionic**, **covalent**, **metallic**, or **van der Waals forces**.
 
 
 
• **Physical Properties:**
 
 
• **Density:** Most substances are at their **highest density** in the solid phase (**ice** is a notable exception due to its unique **hydrogen bonding** structure).
 
• **Diffusion:** The **rate of diffusion** in solids is **extremely low** because particles are not free to move across large distances.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Phase Transitions:** The process of a solid turning into a liquid is called **melting**, while the direct transition from a solid to a gas is known as **sublimation** (e.g., **dry ice** or **naphthalene**).
 
• **Elasticity vs. Plasticity:** Some solids can be **deformed** under stress. If they return to their original shape, they are **elastic**; if the deformation is permanent, they are **plastic**.
 
• **Mechanical Strength:** Solids are categorized by their **hardness**, **brittleness**, and **malleability** (the ability to be hammered into **thin sheets**, a common **feature** of metals like **gold** and **silver**).

questions.question: According to Bohr’s model of an atom, the ‘M’ shell is represented by the principal quantum number ‘n’ equal to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bohr’s Model** of an atom, proposed by **Neils Bohr** in **1913**, postulates that electrons revolve around the nucleus in certain stable, circular paths called **orbits** or **shells**.
 
• These orbits are associated with fixed amounts of energy and are called **energy levels** or **energy shells**.
 
• The shells are represented by the letters **K, L, M, N, ...** or by the **principal quantum number (n)**, where **n** is an integer (**1, 2, 3, 4, ...**).
 
• The shell closest to the nucleus is the **K shell**, for which **n = 1**. The next shell is the **L shell** with **n = 2**.
 
• The **M shell** is the third orbit from the nucleus, and thus it is represented by the **principal quantum number n = 3**. ***Hence, the statement regarding M shell being represented by n equal to 3 is correct.***
 
• The **N shell** follows the M shell and is represented by **n = 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maximum Electron Capacity**: The maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in a shell is calculated using the formula **2n²**, where **n** is the **principal quantum number**.

 
 
• For the **K shell (n=1)**: 2(1)² = **2 electrons**.
 
• For the **L shell (n=2)**: 2(2)² = **8 electrons**.
 
• For the **M shell (n=3)**: 2(3)² = **18 electrons**.
 
• For the **N shell (n=4)**: 2(4)² = **32 electrons**.
 
 
 
• **Energy Levels**: As the value of **n** increases, the distance of the shell from the nucleus increases, and the **energy** associated with that shell also increases. Therefore, the **M shell** has higher energy than the **L shell** but lower energy than the **N shell**.
 
• **Stability**: According to Bohr, electrons do not radiate energy while revolving in these **discrete orbits**. An atom radiates or absorbs energy only when an electron jumps from one energy level to another.
 
• **Octet Rule**: The outermost shell of an atom cannot accommodate more than **8 electrons**, even if it has the capacity to hold more (except for the K shell, which holds a maximum of 2).
 
• **Scientific Contribution**: **Neils Bohr** was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1922** for his work on the structure of atoms. His model helped overcome the limitations of the **Rutherford model** regarding atomic stability.

questions.question: The regular changes in the ovary and uterus during egg formation is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**menstrual cycle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **menstrual cycle** is a series of natural, rhythmic physiological changes that occur in the **female reproductive system** (specifically in **primates** like humans, monkeys, and apes) to make pregnancy possible.
 
• This cycle involves regular changes in both the **ovary** (production of eggs/ovocytes) and the **uterus** (preparation of the lining for a potential embryo).
 
• The average duration of a menstrual cycle is **28 days**, although it can vary between **21 and 35 days** in healthy adults.
 
• The cycle is characterized by the shedding of the **uterine lining (endometrium)**, which results in **menstruation** (bleeding) if fertilization does not occur.
 
• It is regulated by the complex interplay of hormones from the **hypothalamus**, **pituitary gland**, and the **ovaries**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Estrous Cycle**:

 
 
• Unlike the menstrual cycle, the **estrous cycle** occurs in **non-primate mammals** such as **cows, dogs, and cats**.
 
• In this cycle, the **endometrium** is reabsorbed by the body if fertilization does not take place, rather than being shed as blood.
 
• Animals with an estrous cycle are generally only sexually active during the **"heat"** or **estrus** phase.
 
 
 
• **Circadian Rhythm**:
 
 
• This refers to the **24-hour internal clock** in our brain that regulates cycles of **sleepiness and alertness**.
 
• It responds primarily to **light and darkness** in an organism's environment and is not directly responsible for egg formation.
 
 
 
• **Menarche and Menopause**:
 
 
• **Menarche** is the term used for the **first menstrual cycle**, which typically occurs during **puberty** between the ages of **11 and 15**.
 
• **Menopause** marks the **end of reproductive phases** in women, usually occurring between the ages of **45 and 55**, where menstrual cycles cease permanently.
 
 
 
• **Fertilisation cycle**:
 
 
• This is not a standard biological term for the regular monthly changes; rather, **fertilisation** is a singular event where the **sperm** meets the **ovum**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Phases of the Menstrual Cycle**:

 
 
• **Menstrual Phase (Days 1-5)**: The **endometrium** is shed, and **menstrual flow** occurs due to low levels of **progesterone**.
 
• **Follicular Phase (Days 1-13)**: **Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)** stimulates the growth of **ovarian follicles**. The lining of the **uterus** regenerates.
 
• **Ovulatory Phase (Day 14)**: A sudden surge in **Luteinizing Hormone (LH)** causes the **mature follicle** to rupture and release the **egg (ovum)**. This process is called **ovulation**.
 
• **Luteal Phase (Days 15-28)**: The ruptured follicle transforms into the **corpus luteum**, which secretes **progesterone** to prepare the **uterus** for implantation.
 
 
 
• **Hormonal Control**:
 
 
• **Estrogen**: Responsible for the **proliferation** of the uterine lining and secondary sexual characteristics.
 
• **Progesterone**: Essential for **maintaining** the thickened uterine lining during pregnancy.
 
• **LH and FSH**: Pituitary hormones that trigger the **maturation of follicles** and the act of **ovulation**.

questions.question: The sexually transmitted disease AIDS is caused by which of the following?
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Virus**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **AIDS** stands for **Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome**. It is a chronic, potentially life-threatening condition caused by the **Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)**.
 
• By damaging the **immune system**, **HIV** interferes with the body's ability to fight infection and disease. It specifically targets and destroys **CD4 cells** (also known as **T-helper cells**), which are vital for the immune response.
 
• The causal agent of **AIDS** is a **Virus**. **HIV** is a member of the **Retrovirus** family, which means it uses **RNA** as its genetic material and employs an enzyme called **reverse transcriptase** to integrate into the host's **DNA**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Helminths** are multi-cellular parasitic worms, such as **roundworms** and **tapeworms**, that cause diseases like **Ascariasis** or **Filariasis**. They are not the cause of **AIDS**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Protozoa** are single-celled organisms that cause illnesses such as **Malaria**, **Amoebiasis**, and **Kala-azar**. They do not lead to the development of **AIDS**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Bacteria** are prokaryotic microorganisms responsible for diseases like **Tuberculosis**, **Cholera**, and **Typhoid**. While some **sexually transmitted diseases (STDs)** like **Syphilis** are bacterial, **AIDS** is not. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Virus.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Modes of Transmission:**

 
 
• **HIV** is transmitted through contact with infected **blood**, **semen**, or **vaginal fluids**. The most common route is unprotected **sexual contact**.
 
• It can also spread by sharing **contaminated needles** and syringes, or through **blood transfusions** if the blood has not been screened. Transmission from **mother to child** can occur during **pregnancy**, **childbirth**, or **breastfeeding**.
 
 
 
• **Diagnostic Procedures:**
 
 
• The primary screening test for **HIV** is the **ELISA** (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay) test, which detects **antibodies** against the virus.
 
• A positive **ELISA** result is usually confirmed using a more specific test known as the **Western Blot** test. In recent years, **p24 antigen** tests and **Nucleic Acid Tests (NAT)** are also used for early detection.
 
 
 
• **Stages of Infection:**
 
 
• The infection progresses through stages: **Acute HIV Infection**, **Clinical Latency** (Chronic HIV), and finally **AIDS**, which is the most severe phase.
 
• A person is diagnosed with **AIDS** when their **CD4 cell count** drops below **200 cells/mm3** or when they develop certain **opportunistic infections** like **Pneumocystis pneumonia** or **Kaposi's sarcoma**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global and National Context:**

 
 
• **World AIDS Day** is observed annually on **December 1st** to raise awareness and mourn those who have died from the disease. It was first conceived in **1988**.
 
• In **India**, the **National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO)**, established in **1992**, is the nodal agency for formulating policy and implementing programs for the prevention and control of **HIV/AIDS**.
 
 
 
• **Treatment and Management:**
 
 
• There is currently no cure for **HIV/AIDS**, but it can be managed with **Antiretroviral Therapy (ART)**. **ART** involves taking a combination of medicines every day that prevent the virus from multiplying.
 
• Effective **ART** can reduce the **viral load** to undetectable levels, meaning the person can live a long life and has effectively no risk of transmitting the virus through sex.
 
• The **incubation period** (the time from infection to the development of **AIDS**) can range from **5 to 10 years** or more depending on the individual's health and treatment status.

questions.question: A girl clapped her hands near a cliff and heard the echo after 4 s. What is the distance of the cliff from the girl if the speed of the sound is taken as 320 { m s}⁻¹ ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**640 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **echo** is the phenomenon where a sound is heard again after it is reflected back from a distant obstacle, such as a **cliff**, a mountain, or a large wall.
 
• When a person claps their hands near a **cliff**, the sound travels from the person to the cliff and then reflects back to the person's ears. Therefore, the **total distance** covered by the sound is **twice** the actual distance between the person and the cliff.
 
• In this problem, the **speed of sound** (v) is given as **320 m/s** and the **time interval** (t) for the echo to be heard is **4 s**.
 
• The formula to calculate the distance is: **Total Distance = Speed of Sound x Time**. Here, Total Distance = **320 m/s x 4 s = 1280 m**.
 
• Since this **1280 m** represents the distance of the "to-and-fro" journey, the **distance of the cliff** (d) from the girl is half of the total distance.
 
• **Calculation**: d = 1280 / 2 = **640 m**. ***Hence, the correct option is 640 m.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Sound Waves**: Sound is a **mechanical wave** that requires a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel. It travels fastest in **solids** and slowest in **gases**.
 
• **Speed of Sound**: The speed of sound in air is approximately **344 m/s** at a **temperature** of **22 degrees Celsius**. The speed increases with an increase in **temperature** and **humidity**.
 
• **Reflection of Sound**: Just like light, sound follows the **laws of reflection**, where the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection, and they lie in the same plane.
 
• **Applications of Echo**: The principle of echo is used in **SONAR** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) to measure the **depth of the ocean** or locate underwater objects. It is also used by **bats** and **dolphins** for **echolocation** to navigate and find food.
 
• **Medical Use**: **Ultrasonography** uses the reflection of **ultrasonic waves** (sound with frequency above **20,000 Hz**) to create images of internal body organs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Persistence of Hearing**: The sensation of sound persists in our **brain** for about **0.1 seconds**. To hear a distinct echo, the reflected sound must reach the ear after this time interval.
 
• **Minimum Distance for Echo**: For a person to hear a clear echo in air (at **22 degrees Celsius**), the minimum distance of the obstacle from the source of sound should be half of the distance traveled in 0.1 s. Calculation: (344 m/s x 0.1 s) / 2 = **17.2 m**.
 
• **Reverberation**: If the distance is less than **17.2 m**, the reflected sounds overlap with the original sound, causing a prolonged sound effect known as **reverberation**, commonly heard in large **concert halls** or newly built empty rooms.
 
• **Human Auditory Range**: A healthy human ear can typically hear frequencies between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz**. Sounds below 20 Hz are called **infrasonic**, and sounds above 20,000 Hz are called **ultrasonic**.

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are true about the acceleration due to gravity?

(i) The value of acceleration due to gravity depends on the mass of the object falling under the effect of gravity.

(ii) The value of acceleration due to gravity is universally constant.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither (i) nor (ii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration due to gravity (g)** is the acceleration gained by an object due to the **gravitational force** exerted by a massive body like the **Earth**. Its standard value on the Earth's surface is approximately **9.8 m/s²**.
 
• The mathematical formula for acceleration due to gravity is **g = GM / R²**, where **G** is the **Universal Gravitational Constant**, **M** is the **mass of the Earth** (or the celestial body), and **R** is the **radius** of the body.
 
• Statement (i) claims that **g** depends on the **mass of the falling object**. However, the formula **g = GM / R²** shows that the acceleration depends only on the mass and radius of the **planet**, not the object. In a **vacuum**, a feather and a hammer will fall at the same rate. ***Hence, statement (i) is incorrect.***
 
• Statement (ii) claims that **g** is **universally constant**. This is false because **g** varies based on **location**. It is **maximum at the poles** and **minimum at the equator** due to the Earth's **oblate spheroid** shape. It also decreases with an increase in **altitude** (height above Earth) and **depth** (below Earth's surface). ***Hence, statement (ii) is incorrect.***
 
• Since neither of the statements provided in the question is factually accurate regarding the properties of **g**, the correct option is **Neither (i) nor (ii)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Difference between g and G:**

 
 
• **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity**, which is a **vector quantity** and changes from place to place. Its SI unit is **m/s²**.
 
• **G** is the **Universal Gravitational Constant**, which is a **scalar quantity** and remains the same throughout the **universe**. Its value is approximately **6.674 x 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg²**.
 
 
 
• **Weight vs. Mass:**
 
 
• **Mass** is the amount of matter in an object and remains **constant** regardless of location.
 
• **Weight (W = mg)** is the **force** with which an object is attracted towards the center of the Earth. Since **g** varies, the **weight** of an object changes depending on its position in the universe.
 
 
 
• **Gravity on the Moon:**
 
 
• The **mass** and **radius** of the **Moon** are smaller than those of the Earth. Consequently, the acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is about **1/6th** of that on Earth (approx. **1.62 m/s²**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Variation with Shape:** Because the Earth is **flattened at the poles** and **bulged at the equator**, the **equatorial radius** is about **21 km** longer than the **polar radius**. Since **g** is inversely proportional to the square of the radius, it is stronger at the **poles**.
 
• **Variation with Altitude:** As one moves away from the surface of the Earth, the distance from the **center of gravity** increases, causing the value of **g** to **decrease**.
 
• **Variation with Depth:** When moving towards the **center of the Earth**, the effective mass of the Earth attracting the object decreases. At the **center of the Earth**, the value of **g** becomes **zero**.
 
• **Variation due to Rotation:** The **rotation of the Earth** creates a **centrifugal force** that acts outwards, effectively reducing the value of **g**, most significantly at the **equator**.

questions.question: What does variation within a species ensure?

options.text: Better adaptability and chances of survival

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Better adaptability and chances of survival**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Variation** refers to the **morphological**, **physiological**, and **behavioral** differences among individuals belonging to the same **species**.
 
• It ensures **better adaptability** because environments are never static; they undergo constant changes such as **climate shifts**, **resource scarcity**, or the emergence of **new predators**.
 
• Individuals possessing **favorable variations** are more likely to **survive** and **reproduce** in a specific environment, a process central to **Charles Darwin’s** theory of **Natural Selection**.
 
• If all individuals in a population were **genetically identical**, a single adverse change (like a **lethal disease** or **temperature rise**) could potentially wipe out the entire **population**.
 
• **Variation** acts as a buffer, ensuring that at least some individuals have the **traits** necessary to endure **environmental stress**, thereby preventing **extinction**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sources of Variation:**

 
 
• **Genetic Recombination:** Occurs during **meiosis** through **crossing over**, resulting in new combinations of **alleles** in offspring.
 
• **Mutation:** A sudden, stable change in the **DNA sequence**. While some **mutations** are harmful, others introduce **beneficial traits** that drive **evolution**.
 
• **Sexual Reproduction:** The fusion of **gametes** from two different parents ensures **genetic diversity**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Variation:**
 
 
• **Continuous Variation:** Traits that show a range of **phenotypes**, such as **human height** or **skin color**.
 
• **Discontinuous Variation:** Traits that fall into distinct categories, such as **blood groups** (A, B, AB, O) or the ability to roll one's tongue.
 
 
 
• **Importance in Evolution:**
 
 
• **Variation** is the raw material for **evolution**. Over millions of **years**, the accumulation of small variations can lead to **speciation** (the formation of **new species**).
 
• It allows **organisms** to exploit different **ecological niches** and adapt to diverse **geographic locations**.
 
 
 
• **Analysis of Other Options:**
 
 
• **No mutations:** Variation is actually fueled by **mutations**; without them, the **genetic pool** would remain stagnant.
 
• **No evolution:** Variation is the **fundamental requirement** for **evolution**; without it, **evolution** would cease.
 
• **Similar response:** Variation ensures individuals respond **differently** to **environmental changes**, allowing the **fittest** to survive.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **survivability** of an individual depends on whether its **variations** are **adaptive** or **non-adaptive** for its specific **habitat**.
 
• In **asexual reproduction**, variation is minimal and usually occurs only due to **DNA copying errors** or **mutations**.
 
• In **sexual reproduction**, variation is much higher, which is why **sexually reproducing** organisms generally show **greater resilience** to environmental fluctuations.
 
• The study of how **variations** are passed from one **generation** to the next is known as **Genetics**, a field pioneered by **Gregor Mendel** in the **19th century**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are NOT true regarding the work done by a constant force acting on a body?

(i) The work done by the force can never be negative.

(ii) If the direction of the force and displacement of the body is same, the work done will be positive.

(iii) The S.I. unit of work done is Pascal.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Work Done** is defined as the product of the component of the **force** in the direction of the **displacement** and the magnitude of this displacement. Mathematically, it is expressed as **W = Fs cosθ**, where **θ** is the angle between the force vector and the displacement vector.
 
• **Statement (i)**: The work done by a force can indeed be **negative**. This occurs when the **force** acts in a direction opposite to the **displacement** (i.e., the angle **θ** is **180°** or obtuse). A classic example is the **work done by friction** on a sliding body, which is always negative because friction opposes motion. ***Hence, statement (i) is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement (ii)**: When the **force** and **displacement** are in the **same direction**, the angle **θ** is **0°**. Since **cos 0° = 1**, the work done is **positive** and reaches its maximum value (W = Fs). ***Hence, statement (ii) is correct.***
 
• **Statement (iii)**: The **S.I. unit** of work done is the **Joule (J)**, which is equivalent to **1 Newton-meter (N·m)**. **Pascal (Pa)** is the **S.I. unit** for **pressure** or **stress**, defined as one Newton per square meter. ***Hence, statement (iii) is incorrect.***
 
• Since the question asks for statements that are **NOT true**, both **(i) and (iii)** fit the criteria. ***Hence, the correct answer is Both (i) and (iii).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Work**:

 
 
• **Work** is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has only magnitude and no direction, even though both force and displacement are **vector quantities**.
 
• The **dimensional formula** for work is **[ML²T⁻²]**, which is identical to the dimensions of **energy** and **torque**.
 
 
 
• **Zero Work Conditions**:
 
 
• Work done is **zero** if the **displacement is zero** (e.g., pushing against a rigid wall).
 
• Work is zero if the **force is zero**.
 
• Work is zero if the **force is perpendicular** to the displacement (**θ = 90°**). For example, the **centripetal force** acting on a satellite in a circular orbit does **zero work** because it is always perpendicular to the velocity.
 
 
 
• **Units of Work**:
 
 
• In the **CGS system**, the unit of work is the **erg**.
 
• The relationship between the S.I. and CGS units is **1 Joule = 10⁷ ergs**.
 
• Other units include **Kilowatt-hour (kWh)**, often used for electrical energy, where **1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ Joules**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**: It states that the **net work done** by all forces acting on a body is equal to the change in its **kinetic energy**. This is a fundamental principle in **classical mechanics**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct according to the sign convention for spherical lenses?

options.text: Object is always placed on the left of the lens.
Focal length of a concave lens is taken as negative.
Distances measured to the right of the optical centre are positive.
Focal length of a convex lens is taken as negative.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Focal length of a convex lens is taken as negative.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• For **spherical lenses**, we follow the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, where the **optical centre (O)** of the lens is taken as the **origin** and the **principal axis** is taken as the **X-axis**.
 
• According to this convention, the **object** is always placed to the **left** of the lens. This implies that the light from the object falls on the lens from the left-hand side. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **focal length** of a **concave lens** is considered **negative** because its principal focus lies on the left side of the **optical centre**, opposite to the direction of incident light. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• All distances measured to the **right** of the origin (along the positive x-axis) are taken as **positive**, while those measured to the **left** are taken as **negative**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• A **convex lens** is a **converging lens**, and its principal focus is located on the **right side** of the lens. Therefore, according to the sign convention, the **focal length** of a **convex lens** is always **positive**, not negative. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Therefore, the statement "Focal length of a convex lens is taken as negative" is NOT correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lens Formula:** The relationship between the **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by the formula **1/v - 1/u = 1/f**. In this formula, **u** is always **negative** for a real object.
 
• **Magnification (m):** It is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object. For lenses, **m = h'/h = v/u**. A **positive magnification** indicates a **virtual and erect** image, while a **negative magnification** indicates a **real and inverted** image.
 
• **Power of a Lens (P):** The degree of convergence or divergence of light rays achieved by a lens is expressed as its **power**. It is the reciprocal of the **focal length** in metres (**P = 1/f**). The **SI unit** of power is **Dioptre (D)**.
 
• **Sign of Power:** Since the **focal length** of a **convex lens** is positive, its **power** is also **positive**. Conversely, since the **focal length** of a **concave lens** is negative, its **power** is **negative**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Height Measurement:** Distances measured **perpendicularly above** the principal axis (along the +y-axis) are taken as **positive**, which is usually the case for the height of the **object**.
 
• **Inverted Images:** Distances measured **perpendicularly below** the principal axis (along the -y-axis) are taken as **negative**. This applies to the height of **real images**.
 
• **Incident Light Direction:** The convention is designed such that distances measured in the **direction of incident light** are positive, and those measured **against the direction** of incident light are negative.
 
• **Optical Centre:** Every measurement for **spherical lenses** must originate from the **optical centre**, unlike mirrors where measurements start from the **pole**.

questions.question: Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) bears _____ for protein synthesis, while smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) synthesizes _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ribosomes; lipids**__.

 
• The **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** is a large network of membrane-bound tubes and sheets that stretches from the **nuclear envelope** to the **plasma membrane**.
 
• **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)** looks rough under a microscope because it has particles called **ribosomes** attached to its surface.
 
• These **ribosomes** are the primary sites of **protein synthesis** in the cell. The proteins manufactured here are then sent to various places in the cell depending on the need.
 
• **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)** does not have **ribosomes** attached to its surface, giving it a smooth appearance.
 
• The **SER** plays a crucial role in the synthesis of **lipids** (fats) and **steroid hormones**, which are essential for cell function and the building of the **cell membrane**.
 
• Therefore, the correct association is that RER bears **ribosomes** for protein synthesis, while SER synthesizes **lipids**. ***Hence, the correct answer is ribosomes; lipids.***

 
• **Functions of Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER):**

 
 
• In the **liver cells** of vertebrates, **SER** plays a vital role in **detoxifying** many poisons and drugs.
 
• It is also involved in the **metabolism of carbohydrates** and the **storage of calcium ions**, which is particularly important in **muscle cells** (where it is called the sarcoplasmic reticulum) for muscle contraction.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER):**
 
 
• Apart from **protein synthesis**, the **RER** is involved in **protein folding** and quality control, ensuring that only correctly folded proteins proceed to the **Golgi apparatus**.
 
• It provides a large **surface area** for chemical reactions and serves as a pathway for the distribution of materials.
 
 
 
• **Membrane Biogenesis:**
 
 
• Some of the **proteins** and **lipids** synthesized by the ER help in building the **cell membrane**. This process is known as **membrane biogenesis**.
 
• Other proteins and lipids function as **enzymes** and **hormones** throughout the biological system.
 
 
 
• **Structural Components:**
 
 
• The ER membrane is similar in structure to the **plasma membrane** and consists of a **lipid bilayer**.
 
• It exists in three forms: **cisternae** (flattened sacs), **vesicles**, and **tubules**. **RER** is mainly composed of **cisternae**, while **SER** is mainly composed of **tubules**.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes:**
 
 
• These are small, dense, granular structures found either freely in the **cytoplasm** or attached to the **RER**. They are composed of **Ribosomal RNA (rRNA)** and proteins and are known as the "**protein factories**" of the cell.

questions.question: Why does the temperature of ice remain constant during the melting of ice?

options.text: Ice absorbs heat but does not melt
Heat is used to break the bonds between molecules

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heat is used to break the bonds between molecules**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When ice is heated, its temperature rises until it reaches its **melting point**, which is **0°C (273.15 K)** under standard atmospheric pressure.
 
• Once the ice starts to melt, the heat energy supplied is no longer used to increase the **kinetic energy** of the water molecules. Instead, it is used to overcome the **intermolecular forces of attraction** (specifically **hydrogen bonds**) that hold the water molecules in a solid **crystalline structure**. ***Hence, the statement that heat is used to break bonds is correct.***
 
• Since the **average kinetic energy** of the molecules remains unchanged during this process, the **thermometer** shows no rise in temperature until all the ice has completely converted into liquid water.
 
• This absorbed energy, which does not result in a temperature change, is called the **Latent Heat of Fusion**. The word **latent** means "hidden," as this heat is hidden from the temperature scale.
 
• The statement that **ice absorbs heat but does not melt** is scientifically **incorrect** because, at the melting point, the absorption of heat directly causes the phase change from solid to liquid.
 
• The statement that **ice reflects heat** is **incorrect** in this context; while ice has a high **albedo** (reflectivity), the question specifically addresses what happens to the heat that **is** absorbed by the ice.
 
• The statement that **ice becomes denser** is a physical fact (water is denser than ice), but it is a **result** of the molecular bonds breaking, not the **reason** why the temperature remains constant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Latent Heat of Fusion:** For water, the **latent heat of fusion** is approximately **334 Joules per gram** (or **80 calories per gram**). This is the amount of energy required to change **1 gram** of ice at **0°C** to **1 gram** of water at **0°C**.
 
• **Phase Change:** During a **phase change**, the system exists in a state of **thermal equilibrium** where two phases (solid and liquid) coexist. The temperature will only begin to rise again once the **phase transition** is 100% complete.
 
• **Specific Heat Capacity:** Once the ice has completely melted into water, the heat supplied will then increase the temperature of the water based on its **specific heat capacity**, which is **4.184 J/g°C**.
 
• **Molecular Structure:** Ice has a unique **hexagonal lattice** structure. When heat breaks these **molecular bonds**, the molecules actually move closer together in the liquid state, which is why water is more **dense** than ice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kinetic vs. Potential Energy:** In **thermodynamics**, temperature is directly proportional to **average kinetic energy**. During melting, the heat increases the **potential energy** of the molecules (by changing their position and breaking bonds) rather than their speed.
 
• **Effect of Pressure:** The **melting point** of ice can be lowered by increasing the **external pressure**. This phenomenon is known as **regelation**, which allows ice to melt under pressure and refreeze once the pressure is removed.
 
• **Latent Heat of Vaporization:** A similar process occurs when water boils at **100°C**. The temperature remains constant because the heat is used as **Latent Heat of Vaporization** to turn liquid water into **steam**.
 
• **Numerical Value:** The **Latent Heat of Fusion** of water is significantly higher than many other substances, which helps in **regulating the Earth's climate** by slowing the melting of polar ice caps.

questions.question: What happens to the magnetic field strength produced by a circular coil if the number of turns ( n ) is increased while keeping the current constant?

options.text: It becomes n times larger than for a single turn.
It only increases if the diameter is also increased.
It remains the same as for a single turn.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It becomes n times larger than for a single turn**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **magnetic field strength** produced by a **current-carrying circular coil** at its center is directly proportional to the **number of turns (n)** in the coil.
 
• When a **circular coil** has **n turns**, the **current** flows in the same direction in every turn, which means the magnetic field produced by each individual turn adds up vectorially.
 
• For a **single turn**, the magnetic field is produced by the current flowing through that one loop; for **n turns**, the fields of all **n loops** are superposed, resulting in a field that is **n times** as strong.
 
• If the **current (I)** is kept constant, the total magnetic field (**B**) is given by the product of **n** and the field of a single loop. ***Hence, the statement that it becomes n times larger is correct.***
 
• This linear relationship assumes that the turns are tightly wound and the **radius** of the coil remains significantly unchanged for each turn.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mathematical Formula:** The **magnetic field (B)** at the center of a **circular coil** of **radius (r)** carrying **current (I)** with **n turns** is expressed as **B = (μ₀ * n * I) / (2 * r)**, where **μ₀** is the **permeability of free space** (approximately **4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A**).
 
• **Magnetic Field and Current:** The strength of the **magnetic field** is directly proportional to the **magnitude of the current**. If the **current** is doubled, the **magnetic field** also doubles, provided other factors remain constant.
 
• **Inversely Proportional to Radius:** The **magnetic field strength** is inversely proportional to the **radius** of the **circular coil**. A smaller **radius** results in a stronger field at the center because the current-carrying wire is closer to the center point.
 
• **Direction of the Field:** The **direction** of the **magnetic field** produced by a **circular loop** can be determined using the **Right-Hand Thumb Rule**. If the fingers of the right hand curl in the direction of the **current**, the thumb points in the direction of the **magnetic field**.
 
• **SI Unit:** The **SI unit** of **magnetic field strength** or **magnetic flux density** is the **Tesla (T)**. In smaller applications, the unit **Gauss (G)** is also used, where **1 Tesla = 10,000 Gauss**.
 
• **Applications:** This principle is used in the construction of **solenoids**, **electromagnets**, **electric motors**, and **galvanometers**, where increasing the **number of turns** is a common method to amplify **magnetic force** without increasing the **current**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biot-Savart Law:** This fundamental law in **electromagnetism** describes how a **magnetic field** is generated by a steady **electric current**. It is the basis for calculating the field produced by **circular coils**.
 
• **Ampere’s Circuital Law:** Another crucial law used to find the **magnetic field** for highly symmetric current distributions, such as an infinitely long wire or a **toroid**.
 
• **Superposition Principle:** The fact that the field becomes **n times larger** is an application of the **superposition principle**, which states that the total **magnetic field** at any point is the vector sum of the individual fields produced by each segment of the **current**.
