questions.question: Which of the following types of reactions is a neutralisation reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Double displacement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Neutralisation reaction** is a fundamental chemical process where an **acid** and a **base** react with each other to produce **salt** and **water**.
 
• It is categorized as a **Double displacement reaction** (also known as a **metathesis reaction**) because the **cations** and **anions** of the two reacting compounds exchange partners to form new products.
 
• In a typical aqueous neutralisation, the **Hydrogen ions (H+)** from the acid combine with the **Hydroxide ions (OH-)** from the base to form **H2O (water)**.
 
• A standard example of this reaction is **HCl (Hydrochloric acid)** reacting with **NaOH (Sodium hydroxide)** to form **NaCl (Sodium chloride)** and **H2O**. In this case, the **Sodium (Na+)** and **Hydrogen (H+)** ions effectively swap places.
 
• These reactions are usually **exothermic** in nature, meaning they involve the release of **heat energy** during the formation of water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Single displacement reaction:**

 
 
• In this type of reaction, a **more reactive element** displaces a **less reactive element** from its compound.
 
• For example, when **Zinc (Zn)** is added to **Copper sulfate (CuSO4)**, it displaces the copper to form **Zinc sulfate (ZnSO4)** and **Copper (Cu)**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Combustion reaction:**
 
 
• This is a high-temperature **redox reaction** between a fuel and an **oxidant** (usually atmospheric **Oxygen**).
 
• It results in the release of energy in the form of **light** and **heat**, often producing **Carbon dioxide (CO2)** and **Water** as byproducts when hydrocarbons are burned. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Decomposition reaction:**
 
 
• This occurs when a **single reactant** breaks down into **two or more simpler products**.
 
• This process often requires energy in the form of **heat, light, or electricity**. An example is the heating of **Calcium carbonate (CaCO3)** to yield **Calcium oxide (CaO)** and **Carbon dioxide (CO2)**. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Double displacement reaction:**
 
 
• This reaction involves the **exchange of ions** between two compounds to form two new compounds.
 
• The general chemical equation is **AB + CD → AD + CB**. Since a neutralisation reaction involves the **H+** from the acid and **OH-** from the base swapping to form water, while the remaining ions form a salt, it is a classic **Double displacement**. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **pH Levels:** The **pH** of the resulting solution in a neutralisation reaction depends on the strength of the reactants. A reaction between a **strong acid** and a **strong base** results in a neutral salt with a **pH of 7**.
 
• **Applications:** Neutralisation is widely used in **agriculture** to treat **acidic soil** using **slaked lime (Calcium hydroxide)**, and in **medicine** where **Antacids** (bases) are used to neutralise excess **gastric acid** in the stomach.
 
• **Titration:** In **analytical chemistry**, neutralisation reactions are the basis of **acid-base titrations**, which are used to determine the unknown **concentration** of an acidic or basic solution using an **indicator**.

questions.question: What is typically involved in an addition reaction?

options.text: Functional groups are replaced by others
Removal of atoms from molecules takes place
Atoms get added to unsaturated bonds

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atoms get added to unsaturated bonds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **addition reaction** is a fundamental class of chemical reactions where two or more molecules combine to form a **larger single molecule**. This typically occurs in organic compounds containing **multiple bonds**.
 
• In this process, atoms or groups of atoms are **added across the unsaturated bonds** (double or triple bonds) of a molecule, such as **alkenes** or **alkynes**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• During an addition reaction, the **pi (π) bond** of the unsaturated system is broken, and two new **sigma (σ) bonds** are formed. This results in the conversion of an **unsaturated hydrocarbon** into a **saturated** one.
 
• Functional groups being replaced by others is the characteristic of a **substitution reaction**, which is common in **saturated hydrocarbons** like **alkanes**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The removal of atoms from a molecule to form a double or triple bond is known as an **elimination reaction**, which is essentially the reverse of an addition reaction. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• While **oxidation** involves the loss of electrons or increase in oxidation state, an addition reaction specifically focuses on the **structural incorporation** of new atoms into the molecular framework through **covalent bonding**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Addition Reactions:**

 
 
• **Electrophilic Addition:** Commonly seen in **alkenes** and **alkynes**, where an **electrophile** attacks the electron-rich double bond. A classic example is the **halogenation** of **ethene**.
 
• **Nucleophilic Addition:** Typical of compounds containing **carbon-heteroatom** multiple bonds, such as **carbonyl groups** (aldehydes and ketones), where a **nucleophile** attacks the electron-deficient carbon atom.
 
• **Free Radical Addition:** Occurs in the presence of **peroxides** or **UV light**, often following a non-Markovnikov pathway.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogenation:**
 
 
• This is a specific type of addition reaction where **hydrogen gas (H2)** is added to unsaturated compounds in the presence of a **catalyst** like **Nickel (Ni)**, **Palladium (Pd)**, or **Platinum (Pt)**.
 
• Industrial use: It is widely used in the **food industry** to convert **vegetable oils** (unsaturated fats) into **vanaspati ghee** (saturated fats).
 
 
 
• **Bromine Water Test:**
 
 
• Addition reactions are used as a **diagnostic tool** to detect unsaturation. When **bromine water** (reddish-brown) is added to an unsaturated compound, an addition reaction occurs, and the solution becomes **colorless**.
 
 
 
• **Markovnikov's Rule:**
 
 
• In the addition of a protic acid (like **HBr**) to an asymmetric alkene, the **hydrogen atom** attaches to the carbon with the **greater number of hydrogen atoms**, while the halide group attaches to the carbon with more alkyl substituents.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hybridization Change:** In an addition reaction involving an **alkene**, the hybridization of the carbon atoms changes from **sp2 to sp3** as the geometry shifts from planar to tetrahedral.
 
• **Saturated vs Unsaturated:** **Saturated compounds** contain only single bonds and are generally less reactive, whereas **unsaturated compounds** contain **double (C=C)** or **triple (C≡C) bonds**, making them highly susceptible to addition.
 
• **Atom Economy:** Addition reactions are considered highly efficient in **green chemistry** because they have a **100% atom economy**; all atoms in the reactants are present in the final product, leaving no waste or byproducts.
 
• **Polymerization:** Addition **polymerization** is a critical industrial process where thousands of **monomer** molecules (like **ethylene**) undergo repeated addition reactions to form **polymers** (like **polyethylene**).

questions.question: The sulphide ores of metals, which lie in the middle of activity series, are first converted to oxides. The necessary condition for this conversion is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**presence of excess air**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of converting **sulphide ores** into oxides by heating them strongly in the **presence of excess air** is known as **Roasting**.
 
• Metals that lie in the **middle of the activity series**, such as **Zinc (Zn)**, **Iron (Fe)**, and **Lead (Pb)**, are often found in nature as **sulphides** or **carbonates**.
 
• It is much easier to obtain a metal from its **oxide** than from its sulphide; therefore, the sulphide ore must be **oxidized** before **reduction** can occur.
 
• A classic example of **Roasting** is the treatment of **Zinc Blende (ZnS)**. When heated in **excess air**, it reacts to form **Zinc Oxide (ZnO)** and releases **Sulphur Dioxide (SO2)** gas. The chemical equation is: **2ZnS + 3O2 → 2ZnO + 2SO2**.
 
• In this process, **Oxygen** acts as the oxidizing agent to remove the **Sulphur** impurities in the form of volatile gas. ***Hence, the condition of excess air is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Calcination:** Unlike roasting, **Calcination** is the process used for **carbonate ores**. It involves heating the ore strongly in the **absence of oxygen** or a **limited supply of air** to expel carbon dioxide. For example, **ZnCO3 (Calamine)** is heated to produce **ZnO** and **CO2**.
 
• **Reactivity Series:** The metals in the **middle of the series** (like **Zn, Fe, Pb**) are moderately reactive. Metals at the **top** (like **Na, Ca, Mg**) are extracted by **electrolysis**, while metals at the **bottom** (like **Au, Ag**) are often found in a **native state**.
 
• **Reduction:** Once the ore is converted to a **metal oxide**, it is reduced to the free metal using a **reducing agent** like **Carbon (Coke)**. This is a crucial step in **pyrometallurgy**.
 
• **Sulphur Dioxide Management:** The **SO2** gas produced during the **Roasting** of sulphide ores is a major air pollutant but is often collected and used in the **Contact Process** to manufacture **Sulphuric Acid (H2SO4)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Temperature Control:** During **Roasting**, the temperature must be maintained **below the melting point** of the metal or the ore to prevent the mass from fusing together, which would hinder the **oxidation** process.
 
• **Removal of Volatile Impurities:** Apart from converting sulphides to oxides, Roasting also helps in removing **moisture** and organic matter, as well as volatile impurities like **Arsenic** and **Antimony** in the form of their oxides.
 
• **Specific Ores:** Common sulphide ores subjected to roasting include **Galena (PbS)** for Lead, **Copper Pyrites (CuFeS2)** for Copper, and **Cinnabar (HgS)** for Mercury.
 
• **Chemical Nature:** Roasting is an **exothermic process** because the oxidation of metal sulphides releases a significant amount of **thermal energy**, which helps maintain the high temperature required for the reaction.

questions.question: An employee claims ₹20 for each kilometre when he travels by taxi and ₹10 for each kilometre if he travels by his own car. In one week, he claimed ₹2,200 for travelling 120 km. How many kilometres did he travel by taxi?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average rate for the whole **week** = 2200 ÷ 120 = 55/3 per km.

Using **Alligation**: (Taxi rate: 20) and (Car rate: 10) with mean (55/3).

Distance Ratio (Taxi : Car) = (55/3 − 10) : (20 − 55/3) = 25/3 : 5/3 = 5 : 1.

Total units = 5 + 1 = 6 units → 120 km ⇒ 1 unit = 20 km.

**Taxi distance** = 5 × 20 = 100 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Rate for **taxi** = ₹20/km, Rate for **car** = ₹10/km, Total **distance** = 120 km, Total **claim** = ₹2,200.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf555dc3361ffa88164ae8e3e27ae2d052cbae5e500d54f8fe673689fa6d1eae.png] 

Let the distance traveled by **taxi** be x km.

Then, the distance traveled by **own car** = (120 − x) km.

⇒ Total Claim = (Rate × Distance)Tₐₓᵢ + (Rate × Distance)Cₐᵣ

⇒ 2200 = 20 × x + 10 × (120 − x)

⇒ 2200 = 20x + 1200 − 10x

⇒ 2200 − 1200 = 10x

⇒ 1000 = 10x

⇒ x = 100 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

The average value of a mixture is given by A = (n₁v₁ + n₂v₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n represents quantity and v represents the rate.

Rule of Alligation

It is a shorter way to find the ratio in which two ingredients at given prices must be mixed to produce a mixture at a given price: (Quantity of Cheaper) ÷ (Quantity of Dearer) = (CP of Dearer − Mean Price) ÷ (Mean Price − CP of Cheaper).

Linear Equations in One Variable

Problems involving two unknown quantities related by a total sum can always be simplified to a single variable equation by substituting (Total − x) for the second quantity.

questions.question: The average age of 48 students of a class is 19 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 20 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:

questions.question: A car covers three successive 20 km distances at speeds of 10 km/hr, 20 km/hr and 40 km/hr, respectively. Its average speed (in km/hr) is:

__Shortcut Trick__

When **equal distances** (d) are covered at speeds a, b, and c, use the **Harmonic Mean** formula.

Average Speed = 3abc ÷ (ab + bc + ca)

Average Speed = (3 × 10 × 20 × 40) ÷ (200 + 800 + 400) = 24000 ÷ 1400

Average Speed = 240 ÷ 14 = 120 ÷ 7 = 17(1/7) km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 17(1/7) km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Three successive distances = 20 km each. Speeds = 10 km/hr, 20 km/hr, 40 km/hr.

⇒ Average Speed = 60 ÷ (7/2) = (60 × 2) ÷ 7 = 120/7

⇒ Average Speed = 17(1/7) km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 17(1/7) km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

When two equal distances are covered at speeds u and v, the average speed is given by (2uv) ÷ (u + v).

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the **opposite direction**, relative speed is the sum of their speeds (s₁ + s₂). For the **same direction**, it is the difference (s₁ − s₂).

questions.question: The ratio of length, breadth and height of a cuboid box is in the ratio 5 : 4 : 4 while the areas of the three adjacent faces of a cuboidal box are 160 cm² , 64 cm² and 40 cm² , respectively. Find the lateral surface area of the box (in cm² ).

questions.question: If Akhil is as much older than Vijay as he is younger than Karthik, and sum of the ages of Vijay and Karthik is 84 years, then find the age of Akhil.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When one person's age is the **arithmetic mean** of two others, the middle person's age is simply the average of the other two.

Age of **Akhil** = (Sum of ages of **Vijay** and **Karthik**) ÷ 2

⇒ A + A = K + V

⇒ 2A = K + V

⇒ 2A = 84

⇒ A = 84 ÷ 2 = 42

questions.question: The sum of three numbers is 270. If the ratio of the second number to the first number is 2:12 and that of the third number to the second number is 5:10, then find the second number.

Simplify ratios: **Second : First** = 2:12 = 1:6 and **Third : Second** = 5:10 = 1:2.

Combine: **First : Second : Third** = (6×2) : (1×2) : (1×1) = 12 : 2 : 1.

Total units = 12 + 2 + 1 = 15 units → 270.

1 unit = 270 ÷ 15 = 18.

**Second number** = 2 units = 2 × 18 = 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of numbers = 270. Ratio **N₂ : N₁** = 2:12. Ratio **N₃ : N₂** = 5:10.

⇒ To equalize **N₂**, multiply first ratio by 2: **N₁ : N₂** = 12 : 2.

⇒ Combined ratio **N₁ : N₂ : N₃** = 12 : 2 : 1.

⇒ Sum of ratios = 12 + 2 + 1 = 15 parts.

⇒ 15 parts = 270.

⇒ 1 part = 270 ÷ 15 = 18.

⇒ **Second number (N₂)** = 2 parts = 2 × 18 = 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Ratio

When ratios A:B and B:C are given, the combined ratio A:B:C is found by making the common term B equal in both sets.

questions.question: In a quadrilateral IJKL, angle I = 11^circ and angle J = 79^circ . The bisectors of angle K and angle L meet at Z. What is the measure of angle LZK ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The angle formed by the **bisectors of two adjacent angles** of a quadrilateral is equal to **half the sum of the other two interior angles**.

∴ ∠LZK = (∠I + ∠J) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠LZK = (11° + 79°) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠LZK = 90° ÷ 2 = 45°

**∴ The correct answer is 45°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In quadrilateral **IJKL**:

∠I = 11°

∠J = 79°

**Formula Used:**

• Sum of all interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360°

• Sum of angles of a triangle = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ac51ac796e1debf294f8226af573dc31d137ae71309223ba5810f94ba8759ed6.png] 

**Calculations:**

In quadrilateral **IJKL**, the sum of all interior angles is 360°:

⇒ ∠I + ∠J + ∠K + ∠L = 360°

Substitute the given values of ∠I and ∠J:

⇒ 11° + 79° + ∠K + ∠L = 360°

⇒ 90° + ∠K + ∠L = 360°

⇒ ∠K + ∠L = 360° − 90°

⇒ ∠K + ∠L = 270°

Since **KZ** and **LZ** are the angle bisectors of ∠K and ∠L respectively:

⇒ ∠ZKL = ∠K ÷ 2

⇒ ∠ZLK = ∠L ÷ 2

In ▵**LZK**, the sum of angles is 180°:

⇒ ∠LZK + ∠ZKL + ∠ZLK = 180°

⇒ ∠LZK + (∠K ÷ 2) + (∠L ÷ 2) = 180°

⇒ ∠LZK + (∠K + ∠L) ÷ 2 = 180°

Substitute the value of (∠K + ∠L = 270°):

⇒ ∠LZK + (270° ÷ 2) = 180°

⇒ ∠LZK + 135° = 180°

⇒ ∠LZK = 180° − 135°

⇒ ∠LZK = 45°

**∴ The correct answer is 45°.**

**Option Analysis:**

• **Option (1) 31°:** Incorrect, as the calculated value of ∠LZK is 45°, not 31°.

• **Option (2) 45°:** Correct, as verified by the angle sum properties of quadrilaterals and triangles.

• **Option (3) 55°:** Incorrect, as the calculated value of ∠LZK is 45°, not 55°.

• **Option (4) 51°:** Incorrect, as the calculated value of ∠LZK is 45°, not 51°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Bisector Theorem in Quadrilaterals

The angle formed by the bisectors of two adjacent angles of a quadrilateral is always equal to half the sum of the remaining two angles. For quadrilateral IJKL, ∠LZK = (∠I + ∠J) ÷ 2.

Sum of Interior Angles of a Polygon

The sum of the interior angles of any n-sided polygon is given by the formula (n − 2) × 180°. For a quadrilateral (n = 4), the sum is (4 − 2) × 180° = 360°.

Angle Bisectors of Opposite Angles

The angle between the bisectors of two opposite angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the difference of the other two angles.</p

questions.question: In May 2025, which state / union territory government mandated rooftop sprinkler systems on high-rise buildings?

p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of NCT of Delhi** issued a significant mandate in **May 2025** requiring the installation of **rooftop sprinkler systems** on all **high-rise buildings**.
 
• The primary objective of this directive is to mitigate the intense **Urban Heat Island (UHI)** effect that significantly raises temperatures in the capital during peak **summer months**.
 
• This decision was spearheaded by the **Delhi Disaster Management Authority (DDMA)** as part of its updated **Heat Action Plan** to enhance **urban resilience** against record-breaking temperatures.
 
• The mandate applies to both **residential and commercial** high-rise structures, requiring them to utilize automated or manual sprinkler systems to cool building surfaces.
 
• By cooling the exterior of the buildings, the initiative aims to reduce the **indoor cooling load**, thereby decreasing the overall **electricity demand** for air conditioning across the city.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Urban Heat Island (UHI) Effect**:
 
 
• This phenomenon occurs when urban areas experience much higher temperatures than surrounding rural areas due to **concrete surfaces**, **dense infrastructure**, and high **anthropogenic heat**.
 
• In **Delhi**, the UHI effect has been known to cause temperature differences of **5 to 10 degrees Celsius** compared to neighboring forested or rural regions.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Disaster Management Authority (DDMA)**:
 
 
• Established under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, the DDMA is the apex body for disaster planning and response in the **National Capital Territory**.
 
• The authority is chaired by the **Lieutenant Governor of Delhi**, with the **Chief Minister** serving as the Vice-Chairperson.
 
 
 
• **Heat Action Plan (HAP)**:
 
 
• The HAP is a comprehensive framework that includes **early warning systems**, public awareness campaigns, and long-term **mitigation strategies** like **cool roofs** and **afforestation**.
 
• The 2025 update specifically introduced **active cooling technology**, such as the rooftop sprinkler mandate, to deal with **extreme heatwaves**.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Urban Development**:
 
 
• Mandating sprinklers is aligned with **green building norms**, encouraging developers to integrate **sustainable water management** into urban architecture.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Water Sourcing**: To ensure the sustainability of the project, the mandate suggests that building owners should use **treated wastewater** from **Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs)** or **rainwater harvesting** systems instead of fresh potable water.

questions.question: In the 2025 Uttarakhand flash flood that occurred on 5 August 2025, which Himalayan village on the route to Gangotri Dham was devastated by a torrent of water, mud and debris?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharali in Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dharali village**, located in the **Uttarkashi district** of **Uttarakhand**, witnessed a devastating flash flood on **5 August 2025**. The event was triggered by intense **cloudbursts** in the higher reaches of the **Himalayas**, causing the **Kheer Ganga** rivulet to overflow with immense force.
 
• The village is a significant transit point situated on the **Gangotri National Highway (NH-34)**, approximately **20 kilometers** before the **Gangotri Dham**. It is famous for its **apple orchards** and its proximity to the **Bhagirathi River**.
 
• The **2025 flash flood** caused a massive torrent of **water, mud, and debris** to sweep through the settlement, leading to the burial of several houses and the blockage of the **National Highway**. This disaster disrupted the **Char Dham Yatra**, leaving hundreds of pilgrims stranded.
 
• Historically, **Dharali** and surrounding areas like **Harsil** have been vulnerable to such ecological disturbances due to their **geographical location** in the **High Himalayan zone**, where steep slopes and loose soil contribute to rapid **debris flows** during monsoon seasons.
 
• **Joshimath** is located in the **Chamoli district** and is primarily known for **land subsidence** issues rather than being on the direct route to **Gangotri Dham**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Balta** is a village in the **Almora district**, which is part of the **Kumaon division**, whereas the flood occurred in the **Garhwal division**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Rudraprayag** is a district headquarters at the confluence of the **Alaknanda** and **Mandakini** rivers, serving as the gateway to **Kedarnath**, not the specific village devastated on the **Gangotri** route in this context. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uttarkashi District:** Established on **24 February 1960**, it is one of the northernmost districts of **India**, sharing an international border with **Tibet (China)**. It houses the origins of the **Ganga (at Gangotri)** and **Yamuna (at Yamunotri)** rivers.
 
• **Gangotri Dham:** One of the four sites in the **Chota Char Dham** pilgrimage. The temple is dedicated to **Goddess Ganga** and is located at an elevation of **3,100 meters**. The region is ecologically sensitive and falls under the **Gangotri National Park** administration.
 
• **Cloudburst Dynamics:** A **cloudburst** is an extreme amount of precipitation in a short period (usually exceeding **100 mm per hour**). In the **Himalayas**, these are frequent during the **monsoon months** (**July to September**) due to the orographic lifting of moisture-laden winds.
 
• **Harsil Valley:** Located very close to **Dharali**, **Harsil** is known as the "**Mini Switzerland of India**." It sits at an altitude of **2,620 meters** and is inhabited by the **Bhotia tribe**. The area is critical for **border security** and **tourism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Disaster Management:** Following the **2025 flood**, the **State Disaster Response Force (SDRF)** and **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** conducted extensive operations. Under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, the district administration is empowered to evacuate vulnerable zones.
 
• **Geological Vulnerability:** The **Main Central Thrust (MCT)** passes through the **Uttarkashi** region, making it seismically active (Zone V) and prone to **landslides**. The **1991 Uttarkashi earthquake** (magnitude **6.8**) remains one of the most significant tectonic events in this area.
 
• **National Highway 34:** This highway connects **Rishikesh** to **Gangotri**. Constant maintenance is required due to the fragile **shale and schist** rock formations that frequently collapse during heavy rains.
 
• **Ecological Impact:** The accumulation of **debris** in the **Bhagirathi River** can lead to the formation of temporary **artificial lakes**, which pose a downstream threat of **Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOF)** or flash floods if the blockages burst suddenly.
